clue.text: Silly mens' design initially represented in a silly way

indicators.note: represented in the sense of shown in another form, so these letters are rearranged
initially means only the first letter of the word design is used

explanation.surface: A complaint that some men's foolish design was portrayed in a foolish fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' looks like a comment on the design but is fodder: SILLY + MENS + D (first of design), rearranged by 'represented'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without thought is acting foolishly, so the adverb matches 'in a silly way'.

clue.text: A European gathering brings in one by air

indicators.note: brings in says the gathering word takes the numeral inside it

parts.note: a rally is a mass gathering of people
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A meeting of Europeans welcomes a single person who has flown in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done through the air or from aircraft is done by air, an adverbial synonym.

clue.text: Routine work applied to a nervous condition

parts.note: a chore is a routine household task

explanation.surface: Daily drudgery blamed for causing someone's nerves to fray.
explanation.definitionFit: Chorea is a medical disorder of involuntary jerky movements, a disease of the nervous system.

clue.text: Understanding note carried by witch

indicators.note: carried by means held inside the witch word

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old woman or witch

explanation.surface: A witch carries a message she understands.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the knack of something is to have a grasp of it, an idiomatic sense of comprehension.

clue.text: Estimates it upset multiple groups losing time

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the letters upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: 'it' in crosswords means sex appeal, abbreviated SA

indicators.note: multiple says the shortened groups word appears more than once, here twice
losing says a letter is dropped from the groups word

parts.note: sets are groups of things

explanation.surface: A pollster reckons something has unsettled several factions so much they have lost track of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses SA to AS; SETS losing T gives SES, and 'multiple' doubles it to SESSES.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to judge a value, which is what an appraiser does; same verb form.

clue.text: Spot glam rock band ditching the hoop

indicators.note: ditching means throwing away those words from the band's name

parts.note: Mott the Hoople were a 1970s British glam rock band
taken as written from the clue

explanation.surface: Someone picks out a glam rock group that has abandoned its hula hoop.
explanation.walkthrough: Mott the Hoople were a 1970s British glam rock band (All the Young Dudes); take THE HOOP out of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot is to mark with patches or blotches of colour, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Degrees for one engaged in extra writing

indicators.note: engaged in means fitted inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is writing added after a letter
for one means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: Someone working on degree coursework writes extra essays.
explanation.definitionFit: A peg is a step or level, as in taking someone down a peg, so pegs are degrees.

clue.text: It amplifies opening of much in radio communications

definitions.text: opening of much in radio communications
definitions.meaning: the first letter of much is M, which in the NATO radio alphabet is spoken as this word

explanation.surface: A device boosts the start of a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: M, the opening of 'much', is said as this codeword in the NATO phonetic alphabet used in radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A microphone is the short form, and it boosts sound for a speaker; a familiar abbreviation.

clue.text: How the boss speaks — displays of lapidary language?

definitions.meaning: the boss is the head, so his voices are the ...
lapidary means engraved in stone, so the inscribed slabs on graves display it

explanation.surface: A question about how a manager talks, and about polished, formal language.
explanation.walkthrough: Lapidary describes concise, elegant style, but literally means to do with engraved stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave markers carry carved inscriptions, the most literal lapidary text; split the word and it is the head's tones.

clue.text: Deconstruction of greed I depicted as more emotionally intense

indicators.note: deconstruction means taking apart, so the letters are pulled apart and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A critic dismantling my own greed finds it more raw and intense.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy art or drama is tense and provocative, so a comparative of it is more intense.

clue.text: Good break from work — about to have a meal? Most excellent

indicators.note: about means going round, so the break word encloses the meal word

parts.note: a rest is a break from work
ate means had a meal

explanation.surface: A worker enjoys a good break and is about to eat: the best of times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to have a meal' reads as one phrase meaning 'soon to eat', but 'about' is the container signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of great, which can mean excellent, so it is the top degree of excellence.

clue.text: Source of rumour to have impact on tavern's premier beer

parts.note: to tell is to have a marked effect, as in 'the strain began to tell'

indicators.note: premier means first, so only the opening letter of tavern is taken

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Gossip in the pub about the effect of its best beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gossip who spreads secrets is a source of rumour, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Cheer up religious man (not priest)

indicators.note: not says the priest letters are left out of the churchman

parts.note: a prelate is a bishop or other senior churchman

explanation.surface: An instruction to cheer up a churchman who is not actually ordained.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate someone is to make them happy, the same as raising their spirits.

clue.text: Daughter leaves parties — cheers period of sleep

indicators.note: leaves means goes away from, so that letter is removed

parts.note: sides are parties in a dispute or match
ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: A daughter leaves the parties, says cheers, and goes for a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: A short afternoon nap, especially in hot countries, is a period of sleep.

clue.text: Studies excluding Independent and Conservative from governing body offend

indicators.note: excluding says these party labels are taken out of the earlier words

parts.note: trains means studies or prepares
Congress is the US legislature

explanation.surface: A political grumble: with independents and Tories shut out of the legislature, studies upset people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excluding' takes I from TRAINS and CON from CONGRESS, leaving TRANS + GRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To transgress is to break a rule or give offence, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Retiring after beginning to appear grey

indicators.note: after says the shy word follows the first letter
beginning to means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: a retiring person is shy

explanation.surface: A timid person, once they start to show up, looks pale.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour of ash is pale grey, so the adjective describes greyness.

clue.text: Method answer is presented by Phi?

indicators.note: presented by says the setter's word comes before the answer word

parts.note: Phi is the setter, so from his point of view the word is me

explanation.surface: The setter asks whether his way of solving delivers the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by pseudonym; Phi signed this puzzle, so 'Phi' gives ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A way or method of doing something is a means, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Strangely calm about articles about one? Definitely not calm!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled word goes round the rest
strangely says the four letters of calm are oddly arranged
the second about says the articles surround the numeral

parts.note: an and a are the indefinite articles
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone oddly calm discusses articles about one person: hardly calm.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter reuses 'calm' on purpose: as anagram fodder (with 'Strangely') and in the exclamatory definition. Both 'about's are containers.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild and frenzied behaviour is the opposite of calm, so the exclamation is a fair definition.

clue.text: Who's recalled in memoir as tyrant?

definitions.text: Who's recalled in memoir as tyrant?

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A question about who is remembered as a despot in someone's memoirs.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Who's' alone as the definition, which defines nothing; the whole clue is the definition. Hidden in memoiR AS Tyrant, then read backwards by 'recalled'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian emperor, such as Ivan the Terrible, is the classic autocrat remembered as a tyrant.

clue.text: Involving no payment to feller at work

indicators.note: at work means busy being reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lumberjack is told he works without being paid.
explanation.definitionFit: A freephone number or road costs the user nothing, so it involves no payment.

clue.text: One delivers crushing response: "Limits to party time, love"

indicators.note: limits to means the outer letters of the word party

parts.note: hon, short for honey, is a term of endearment like love

explanation.surface: A put-down in quotation: someone tells their beloved the party must end.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: this snake kills by constriction, so its response is literally crushing.
explanation.definitionFit: A constrictor snake crushes its prey, so a crushing response is its natural reply.

clue.text: Jinx over and over dogging criminal

indicators.note: dogging means following close behind, so the overs come after the criminal

parts.note: a hood is a hoodlum or gangster
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
the second over gives another O

explanation.surface: A curse keeps following a criminal again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodoo is a run of bad luck or a person or thing bringing it, the same as a jinx.

clue.text: Blood circulation problem, some limb being broken

indicators.note: being broken means smashed into pieces, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A doctor notes a circulation problem when a limb is broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockage such as a clot or air bubble lodged in a blood vessel obstructs circulation.

clue.text: Silent movie star's swagger, not needing to retain line

indicators.note: not needing to retain says that letter is dropped

parts.note: bluster is boastful swaggering talk

explanation.surface: A silent film star whose bravado no longer needs scripted lines.
explanation.walkthrough: Buster Keaton was the deadpan star of 1920s silent comedies.
explanation.definitionFit: Buster Keaton is a famous silent film comedian, so his first name stands for the star.

clue.text: Pretentious over crews getting seats

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means showy or excessive
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
mans means staffs or crews, a verb

explanation.surface: Showy staff take over the seating.
explanation.definitionFit: An ottoman is a low upholstered seat or footstool, so the plural are seats.

clue.text: What's final bit of sadism in those people?

parts.note: the question 'what is the final bit of sadism?' is answered 'the M', so What's gives the

indicators.note: final bit of means the last letter of the word sadism

explanation.surface: A question about the cruel streak in some people.
explanation.walkthrough: Answer the riddle: the final bit of 'sadism' is 'the M', run together.
explanation.definitionFit: An object pronoun for a group of others; it can stand for 'those people' in a sentence.

clue.text: Without funds, unable to use name in comedy spot

indicators.note: unable to use says that letter is left out

parts.note: skint is British slang for broke

explanation.surface: A broke comic cannot drop names in a short routine.
explanation.walkthrough: SKINT is everyday British slang for having no money.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic sketch, a spot in a comedy show.

clue.text: Exotic trip not entirely harmless in desert conditions? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means a word with its last letter dropped

parts.note: safe means harmless

indicators.note: the second not entirely cuts the last letter of the dry word too

parts.note: arid describes desert conditions, dry

explanation.surface: An adventure holiday that is not entirely safe in desert heat.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an expedition to see wild animals, typically in Africa, an exotic journey.

clue.text: Bring down activity in media roles

indicators.note: activity suggests the letters are busy moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: Busy media work can sap one's spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishearten someone is to bring their spirits down, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Extract of novel? Seems otherwise

indicators.note: Extract of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A reader asks of a passage from a novel: it seems different?
explanation.definitionFit: Else and otherwise are adverb synonyms, as in 'or else' and 'or otherwise'.
